articleBody:
Before installation day arrives, small oversights can bring work to an immediate standstill. Going through this practical checklist helps ensure your kitchen is fully prepared before heavy slabs arrive at your home.

- [ ] Clear all base cabinets and drawers — Emptying contents protects your cookware and gives installers unobstructed access to cabinet framing and sink cutouts.
- [ ] Have the exact sink and faucet on site — Installers must match mounting hardware, cutout margins, and faucet hole diameters directly to the physical fixtures.
- [ ] Have the cooktop model or physical unit available — Precise cutouts require manufacturer specifications or the appliance itself to avoid trimming stone indoors later.
- [ ] Clear an open pathway through the home — Heavy stone and solid surface slabs require wide, safe transit through exterior doors, hallways, and kitchen corners.
- [ ] Check base cabinet level across all runs — Cabinets must be plumb and secured to wall studs so that heavy surface materials do not bridge hollow gaps.
- [ ] Confirm water supply shut-off valves work — Functional shut-offs under the sink ensure lines can be isolated without shutting down water to the entire home.
- [ ] Plan support brackets for bar overhangs — Extended seating overhangs require pre-installed structural steel brackets to support weight safely.

What to Prepare Before You Start

Use this checklist to walk your space a few days before templating and delivery. Taking care of these items in advance keeps your remodel running smoothly. For comprehensive assistance, contact Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
